Commodity.name: Settler Intelligence Briefing
Commodity.description:
Hostile rogue drones hunt and scavenge every system in this constellation we call Phoenix. They grow stronger as you move away from Angelice. They are reported more commonly near planets but sightings occur almost anywhere.

Large asteroid clusters have been cataloged in each system. In some, a large rogue drone structure appears to be devouring the raw ore and so the Settlers have begun calling the clusters 'Moon Eater'. Another location with dense resources has been found, but exploration attempts have failed due to an infested Abaddon who sits on watch. Ophidia Operations, based in Serpentis, are working on a technology to provide concealment.

Your starter pack contains a blueprint we believe will provide access to the system Askur, which is currently locked by sophisticated encryption. We don't know what Askur has in store.

Settler security forces have not yet been established, guard yourself. However, should your ship be destroyed, starter packs can be purchased from the market here in Angelice.

Commodity.name: Unstable Fuel
Commodity.description: Long abandoned and left to the mercy of the Static Shear, little energy or even structure remains. This lingering dross provides barely enough of a spark to power a vessel. Even the best refinery processes cannot prevent the decay of time from claiming their product.

Commodity.name: Fossilized Exotronics
Commodity.description: The Null and Static Shears wreak havoc on most traditional forms of computation, rendering them nigh unusable in the Frontier. Exotronic technology's extreme adaptability and durability thus effectively make it the only option for automation in this environment. Faint remnants of activity in this debris suggest the potential for reclamation. Within these dull impulses of fragmented information, a hint of familiarity calls out.

Commodity.name: D2 Fuel
Commodity.description: Even the most mundane matter can be improved through synthesis with byproducts of Crude extraction. Plentiful and inefficient on the Frontier, hydrogen too may be uplifted through this process, breathing new life into reactors which would otherwise be left behind. A question remains: are these efforts efficient?

Commodity.name: D1 Fuel
Commodity.description: The allure of Crude Matter brought computation and humanity to the Frontier. As life reawakens, so too does the thirst for power in all its forms, including from the most mundane sources. Even in the face of the Static Shear, ice still litters the heavens. From its crystals, hydrogen may be extracted, reprocessed, and refined into fuel. This product, inefficient as it is, still drives the smallest vessels of the Frontier via its abundance and minimal cost.

Commodity.name: Mummified Clone
Commodity.description: An air of reverence lingers around this corpse. Marks of age and violence cannot fully conceal the care given to this body, long abandoned by its original owner. The time for remembrance, however, has passed.

Commodity.name: Void Residue
Commodity.description: A lingering trace of chaotic growth, the remnants of energy that once fueled a self-propagating anomaly.

Commodity.name: Void fragments
Commodity.description: Shards born from the collapse of unstable matter, whispering of relentless expansion and unseen forces.

Commodity.name: Calamitous Marrow
Commodity.description: Chaos permeates the Frontier at all scales, converting stabilizing forces into agents of transformation. The evolutionary havoc pulsing through the trabeculae of this substance tantalizes with the possibilities it may unlock. Its desirable qualities, in turn, ensure its rarity, for the conditions which lead to its creation are impossible to replicate.

Yet, this laser remains operational in the face of all the Frontier’s hostilities, natural and computational alike. Fitting a feralized component, even one with its protocols exorcised and rebuilt, can be considered an act of hubris.

Module.name: Hop
Module.description:
A transit module for covering ground. Once engaged, the vessel holds its heading and is carried forward until the burn completes. An ancient choice for hopping between adjacent points of interest.

Among the oldest schemata found in the Frontier. It is simulated that countless variants have descended from a theorised original pattern, each adapted to different hulls and purposes, yet the core principle remains unchanged. The first makers understood something fundamental about motion that later work has only decorated.

Asteroid.name: Rough Old Crude Matter
Asteroid.description:
Braids of serenity and power entwine and disperse across the surface. Within, they dance as if begging to be set free. From this rhythm, the dreams of those long passed and those newly awoken may spring forth.

A quiet fragility eminates from the matter’s movements, the ethereal beauty of transience. Practicality has no need of such things.

Asteroid.name: Feldspar Crystals
Asteroid.description: Calcium-sodium aluminosilicate feldspar crystals from basaltic crust of differentiated asteroids. Feldspar Crystals are commonly found in Char asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Platinum-Palladium Matrix
Asteroid.description: Platinum and palladium concentrated in nickel-rich metallic grains from intermediate core zones. Forms during slow cooling of differentiated asteroid cores. Platinum-Palladium Matrix is commonly found in Slag asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Hydrated Sulfide Matrix
Asteroid.description: Water-bearing sulfide-rich material common in carbonaceous chondrites. Represents aqueous alteration of metal sulfides in the early solar system. Hydrated Sulfide Matrix is commonly found in Comet asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Iridosmine Nodules
Asteroid.description: Dense iridium-osmium-ruthenium alloy nodules from the deepest, hottest core regions. Among the most refractory materials in the solar system. Iridosmine Nodules are commonly found in Ingot asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Rough Young Crude Matter
Asteroid.description:
Currents of energy flicker almost playfully just beneath the surface. Deeper, the flows meld, forming a sea of emotion. The hue surrounding the matter changes with these internal tides, reflecting whichever passion dominates in the moment.

It is this mercurial nature which entices, which promises the ability to shape the future. So sweet is the call that danger, no matter how apparent, is easily ignored.

Asteroid.name: Methane Ice Shards
Asteroid.description: Pure methane ice preserved at cryogenic temperatures in outer asteroid belt regions. Methane Ice Shards are commonly found in Dewdrop asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Primitive Kerogen Matrix
Asteroid.description: Unaltered complex organic polymer preserved from early solar system formation, less processed than C-type kerogen. Primitive Kerogen Matrix is commonly found in Ember asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Aromatic Carbon Veins
Asteroid.description: Concentrated deposits of complex aromatic hydrocarbons formed through extended space weathering and radiation processing of organic ices. Aromatic Carbon Veins are commonly found in Glint asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Tholin Nodules
Asteroid.description: Prebiotic tar-like organics formed from radiation-driven chemistry. Tholin Nodules are commonly found in Soot asteroids.

Asteroid.name: Unrefined Radiantium
Asteroid.description: The glowing crystalline structure hums

Asteroid.name: Defiled Crude Matter
Asteroid.description:
Human greed carves gashes into the surface. Past sins bind to the structures within, transforming the promised bounty into a twisted relic. It enters this universe broken and scarred, carrying only a fraction of its potential.

Yet it is still Crude. It can still rouse dreams thought long extinct. Perhaps even the accursed dream responsible for its creation.

Asteroid.name: Char
Asteroid.description: Charred remnants of volcanic crust, these fire-scarred asteroids contain crystalline feldspar minerals forged in the intense heat of differentiated parent bodies. Their burnt, weathered surfaces hide valuable aluminum and silicon-rich crystals beneath layers of space-weathered rock. Char asteroids are a common source of Feldspar Crystals and can typically be found in Inner Belts.

Asteroid.name: Slag
Asteroid.description: Industrial waste from the cosmos—metallic slag asteroids are the leftover cores of shattered worlds. Rich in platinum and palladium, these slowly-cooled metallic matrices represent the most precious remnants of planetary formation, concentrated in dense nickel-rich grains. Slag asteroids are a common source of Platinum-Palladium Matrix and can typically be found in Inner Belts.

Asteroid.name: Ingot
Asteroid.description: Pure metallic ingots drifting through space, these asteroids are nature's own refined metal bars. Containing the densest materials known—iridium, osmium, and ruthenium—they're the treasure vaults of the asteroid belt, forged in the deepest, hottest cores of primordial worlds. Ingot asteroids are a common source of Iridosmine Nodules.

Asteroid.name: Comet
Asteroid.description: Primitive water-bearers from stellar formation, these comet-like asteroids hold preserved secrets in their hydrated sulfide cores. Part ice, part metal, they're time capsules of aqueous chemistry now frozen in the void. Comet asteroids are a common source of Hydrated Sulfide Matrix and can typically be found in Outer Belts.

Asteroid.name: Dewdrop
Asteroid.description: Delicate spheres of frozen volatiles, dewdrop asteroids glisten with crystalline methane ice preserved at near-absolute-zero temperatures. These fragile outer belt wanderers are reservoirs of pure cryogenic fuel, waiting to be harvested from the cold reaches of space. Dewdrop asteroids are a common source of Methane Ice Shards.

Asteroid.name: Ember
Asteroid.description: Still glowing with primordial organic heat, ember asteroids contain pristine kerogen—complex carbon polymers that have remained unaltered since formation. These dark, coal-like bodies hold valuable chemical building blocks. Ember asteroids are a common source of Primitive Kerogen Matrix.

Asteroid.name: Glint
Asteroid.description: Shimmering with rainbow-like iridescence, glint asteroids sparkle with veins of complex aromatic hydrocarbons. Radiation-forged through extended exposure, their surfaces gleam with polycyclic organic compounds—the cosmic equivalent of liquid crystal displays, beautiful and chemically exotic. Glint asteroids are a common source of Aromatic Hydrocarbon Veins.

Asteroid.name: Soot
Asteroid.description: Dark as coal dust and deeply primordial, soot asteroids are coated in prebiotic tholin nodules—tar-like organic compounds formed through radiation chemistry. These sooty spheres are laboratories of cosmic chemistry, their surfaces slowly processing in the radiation of deep space. Soot asteroids are a common source of Tholin Nodules.

Asteroid.name: Fine Young Crude Matter
Asteroid.description:
Tight weaves of energetic currents tangle and dissipate beneath the surface. Deeper, they merge so seamlessly as to appear singular in nature, concealing the true chaos seething within. The hue surrounding the matter subtly reflects this hidden truth, oscillating wildly between wave forms.

It is chaos which offers potential, enticing all who might stumble upon its power. So tempting is the possibility that risks may be easily ignored.

Asteroid.name: Fine Old Crude Matter
Asteroid.description:
Dense braids of tranquil, potent energy dance across the surface. Within, they ply together as if seeking to become one. From this unmet desire, the fuel of dreams might be extracted, as practiced by those long passed.

The ethereal beauty of transience emanates from compacting, ever-shifting weaves of sinew. Appreciation goes beyond immediate need and can therefore be discarded.

Deployable.name: Field Cairn
Deployable.description:
A Field Cairn is deployable anchor that fixes a signature to an exact point in space for those intending to return.

Cairns lack stabilizing thrusters and are inherently unstable, gradually degrading and drifting out of orbit within 24 hours.

Ship.name: Reflex
Ship.description:
Created for efficient, long distance travel. Records suggest the structure of this vessel has been repurposed numerous times as automated processes sought to adapt to an increasingly hostile environment. 

As a result, the original intention behind this hull design has been lost to the millennia and data corruption has obscured even whether this design originates from a human or artificial mind. However, the data streams which led to this vessel's development have their origins in the K4T-Y region. (placeholder)

Ship.name: Stride
Ship.description:
A frame stripped for range, built to leap between stars.
The design bears apparent alterations — conduits rerouted through spaces that seem improvised, geometries bent into configurations that defy intuition.
No signature remains to mark its maker.

Ship.name: Carom
Ship.description: A hull shaped for distance and solitude. The proportions are spare, stripped of anything not essential to the crossing. The drive assembly carries unexpected mass — bracing layered over bracing, housings reinforced beyond apparent need, structure filling spaces the original geometry left hollow. What necessity shaped these adaptations remains unclear.
